html:
The tenge is the currency of Kazakhstan, introduced on 15 November 1993 when the country left the rouble zone. Its name comes from an old Turkic word for a silver coin, the same root as the Russian dengi, "money".

After the Soviet Union dissolved, the new states at first kept the rouble. In 1993 Russia brought in new notes and set hard terms for staying in a shared zone, so Kazakhstan and its neighbours issued money of their own; Kyrgyzstan's som had come earlier that year.

The early tenge lost value fast in the inflation of the 1990s, then steadied as oil money from fields like Tengiz, carried by the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, flowed in. It has been devalued several times when oil prices fell, notably in 2009 and 2014, and in 2015 the central bank let it float freely. Its own currency sign was adopted in 2007. Compare the Mongolian tögrög, another currency of the steppe.
